title: Lexicon Technicum: OR, AN Universal English Dictionary OF ARTS AND SCIENCES
author: John Harris
editions: Volume 1: Fourth Edition (1725); Volume 2: Second Edition (1723)
edition: 4th edition of volume 1 (1725) with 2nd edition of volume 2 (1723)
words_note: words is the total of all record texts in the built data (dictionary entries 1197304 + front matter 8242 + back matter 60169 = 1265715). The cleanup report's cleaned-text total (1,266,244) is superseded: the front-matter repair replaced the garbled front-matter records after the first build. The combined cleaned-text file as it now stands totals 1,265,711 words.
audit_note: 2026-11-27 no-omission audit: 1 wrongly-changed reading restored to the printed text ('Six Isaac Newton' → 'Sir Isaac Newton' ×2, in DEP and ALGEBRA); see lexicon-technicum-1723/audit-restorations.md. No word-count change on the restorations.
letters_note: The book has 24 letter sections in the period alphabet (no J or U sections; J files under I, U under V), but 134 headwords are spelled with J or U (JANITOR, JAUNDICE, UNDUST, UOD, ...), so their lookup keys begin with j or u and the data holds j.json and u.json as well. The site looks an entry up by the first letter of its key; without those two files those 134 entries would be unreachable by search. The words.json row still carries the book's true section (I or V).
corrections_note: 129,349 by the cleanup engine + 4,579 by the sentence context pass (round 1: 1,187; round 2: 135; round 3: 3,257).
unresolved: 21,270 occurrences (19,429 distinct tokens) left as-is, plus 12,651 ambiguous occurrences; see lexicon-technicum-1723-unresolved.md.
citation: The book has no printed page numbers. Cite entries by volume, letter section and headword, never by page.
lost_entries: SECTA facienda per illam quæ habet eniciam partem
SECTA unica tantum facienda pro pluribus hereditatibus
lost_entries_note: Lost entirely to the two-column interleave; recorded as lost, not invented. Their text survives only in fragments inside neighbouring entries. Only SECTA ad Curiam was recoverable as a headword; the other two SECTA entries sit mid-line inside SECRETION. See the cleanup report, section 6.
monsters_note: Table regions and treatise prose the parser could not separate; kept whole as cleaned, not split by guesswork. See the cleanup report, section 6.
z_note: The 1723 vol. 2 reorganised the Z material relative to the 1710 vol. 2: ZOCCO does not occur in any of the three vol. 2 scans, and the 78,726-word SOLAR monster of the 1708-1710 vol. 2 is gone.
